transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Time: 16:30 - 17:04 UTC
Duration: ~34 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Sheikh (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Maple Financial - Head of ML), Raj Patel (Maple - Platform Eng), Sam Reed (Maple - Product)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- Quick hosted API demo covering streaming behavior, generation params, retry/backoff strategies and console hints for cost control.
- Customer is interested in low-latency chat for live-assist and an async summarization pipeline; primary concerns are latency, cost, and audit/SOC2.

Topics covered:
- Streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs
- Parameters (max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop sequences) and safe defaults
- Retry patterns, idempotency and small-request vs batch economics
- Console/Optimize recommendations: caching, batching, quantization suggestions
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, VPC options

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: hi everyone, thanks for joining, im lena from Redwood, im an account exec, and joining me is omar from our infra team. how's everyone doing?
[00:09] Aisha Khan: good thanks, sorry we had a quick run over with infra, should be fine now. excited to see the hosted flow, our use is kind of split between live chat assist and long-form summaries.
[00:20] Lena Park: perfect, high level i will walk through the hosted chat path, streaming behavior, then omar will dive into params, retries and a couple of console tips in optimize for cost.
[00:31] Omar Sheikh: hey, quick note, i'll include a tiny benchmark snippet you can run — it uses curl and a websocket example so you can see streaming latency vs full-response times.
[00:40] Raj Patel: nice, we're particularly sensitive to p99 latency for live assist, and also need to throttle cost on the summarization job.
[00:48] Lena Park: understood. ok jumping in, this is the hosted api - you can do streaming where tokens come over a websocket or sse style stream, that helps perceived latency because the user sees partials, and you can set token chunking.
[01:05] Omar Sheikh: just to add, streaming doesn't mean you lose any control over params — the same max_tokens, temperature, top_p apply. also we have a streaming buffer size you can tune; default's conservative.
[01:17] Sam Reed: couple quick clarifying q's, if we stream and we get a network hiccup mid-turn, what's the retry story?
[01:23] Omar Sheikh: good q. for transient network errors we recommend idempotent request ids for critical flows if you expect retries. typical pattern: generate with a client-side request id, have server respond with final token offsets; on retry the service can either resume from kv cache or return a consistent final response depending on model variant.
[01:40] Aisha Khan: kv cache? we heard about key-value cache in docs but not sure how it fits with hosted.
[01:46] Omar Sheikh: right, its our prefix / KV caching. if you have repeated system prompts or long histories we can cache the KV state so subsequent calls bypass full re-attention work — big cost and latency wins. sometimes our notes say 'K-V cahce' in quick docs, sorry for typos there.
[02:00] Raj Patel: is that enabled per-tenant? we need strict isolation.
[02:04] Lena Park: yes — for hosted API it's per-API key and you can choose to turn caching on or off. for Dedicated/Private you have even more controls.
[02:12] Sam Reed: on params, what's a safe default for temperature for customer-facing chat?
[02:16] Omar Sheikh: 0.2 to 0.6 depending on desired creative-ness. for FAQ/assist you want lower temps. and for long summaries you usually reduce max_tokens and use presence_penalty to avoid repetition.
[02:30] Aisha Khan: curious about token accounting when streaming — are we billed per final token or per streamed char chunk?
[02:36] Lena Park: billed per final generated tokens + prompt tokens. streaming transport doesn't change billing.
[02:42] Raj Patel: ok good. cost controls — you mentioned Optimize in the console?
[02:46] Omar Sheikh: yep, in Console -> Optimize we show token-level breakdowns, suggestions for batching or quantization matches based on your workload. for example the console might recommend int8 quant for your summarization batch jobs, and suggest a batching window for throughput vs latency.
[03:05] Sam Reed: what about the tradeoff of batching for the live assist — we can't hold for 50ms if it increases perceived latency.
[03:11] Omar Sheikh: exactly — small batching windows (like micro-batching 5-10ms) can still be helpful, but for sub-100ms p99 you want near-zero batching and possibly a faster model variant. our smart routing can fallback to a lower-cost variant when the primary is overloaded.
[03:26] Aisha Khan: i want to ask about compliance — we are SOC2 in progress, do you store raw transcripts, and what retention controls exist?
[03:34] Lena Park: hosted stores logs for monitoring but you can configure redaction rules and retention. for regulated flows many customers go with Dedicated or Private where audit logs and KMS integrations are under their control. we have SOC two artifacts we can share.
[03:47] Raj Patel: do you support SSO / SAML for console access and RBAC?
[03:50] Lena Park: yes SAML/SSO and RBAC in Console. also options for customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private.
[03:59] Omar Sheikh: back to retry patterns — common approach is client exponential backoff with jitter, retry on 5xx and network errs but not on 4xx. for streaming partials we suggest rehydrate from last confirmed token if you have the request id, otherwise treat as a full retry and accept re-generation.
[04:18] Sam Reed: do you give a token offset so we can resume mid-stream?
[04:21] Omar Sheikh: depends on transport; websocket streams include token indices in events, SSE variants give partial chunks. we include sequence markers but i'd say this is more an advanced pattern. i'll include example code.
[04:33] Aisha Khan: ok, thinking about our summarization pipeline — we run large batch jobs overnight, can console tell us whether quantization hurts quality?
[04:43] Omar Sheikh: Optimize has quality-monitoring where you can run evals on small prompt sets to see regression risk for quant models. it's not perfect but gives a signal, and we tie alerts to a prompt suite so you catch regressions.
[04:58] Raj Patel: what's the typical delta in latency when going from float16 -> int8 quant?
[05:02] Omar Sheikh: depends on model and hw, often 1.5x-2x throughput increase and token latency drops 20-40% in many cases. concrete numbers in the benchmark guide i'll send.
[05:16] Lena Park: i'm going to demo a quick live generation in the hosted Console — so you can see streaming tokens come in and the console's cost breakdown.
[05:24] [screen share noise / typing]
[05:36] Lena Park: ok, hitting the /chat endpoint with a small system prompt, you can see tokens come in, the latency to first token is about 280ms in this region — this is a dev sandbox; production will vary.
[05:48] Aisha Khan: that feels reasonable, our p99 target is 400ms for shallow assist.
[05:53] Omar Sheikh: with reserved capacity you can tighten that. for hosted, burst capacity and routing to a closer region help.
[06:02] Raj Patel: if we need isolation for data residency later, private deployment is the option?
[06:06] Lena Park: yes private (VPC/on-prem) for residency and full control. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our infra with tenancy guarantees.
[06:15] Sam Reed: any gotchas with idempotency tokens for retries? we've seen double-actions from retries in other vendors.
[06:20] Omar Sheikh: two things — 1) make your upstream handler idempotent (don't perform side-effect operations until model response validated), 2) use client request id and a server-side dedupe store. for streaming, dedupe is trickier but sequence markers help.
[06:36] Aisha Khan: what about rate limits? we want a soft limit that doesn't kill the UX.
[06:41] Lena Park: we have per-key rate limiting and you can request custom limits. also the console exposes token budgets and can alert on near-threshold.
[06:51] Raj Patel: can we do a small POC to measure p95/p99 with our real prompts?
[06:55] Lena Park: absolutely — very standard. we'll provide a benchmark checklist and small harness you can run in your environment. omar will provide the harness.
[07:03] Omar Sheikh: i'll send curl/ws examples and a small python runner; also include a script to capture p50/95/99 and token counts.
[07:11] Sam Reed: timeline wise we want to validate latency with a week and then decide on dedicated vs hosted.
[07:16] Lena Park: sounds doable. quick demo follow-up: in Console -> Optimize you'll see suggested batching window, and an example of prefix caching toggles. if you toggle caching off for a sensitive flow you lose that cost win but retain simpler audit.
[07:33] Aisha Khan: is there a way to redaction at ingest time? we have SSNs and need to strip them.
[07:38] Lena Park: we support pre-ingest redaction rules and post-hoc audit logs. for high-compliance use cases we recommend Private + customer-managed KMS.
[07:48] Raj Patel: curious, any misconceptions customers have about streaming?
[07:51] Omar Sheikh: many assume streaming = cheaper; it's not — billing is token-based. streaming improves perceived latency but compute cost depends on tokens generated and model. also some folks assume streaming solves all retry problems — it helps UX but you still need robust idempotency.
[08:07] Sam Reed: good to know. ok can you recap the ask we should prepare to move forward?
[08:12] Lena Park: sure — we need your traffic histogram + real prompt set, we'll run a mini-benchmark, send you pricing and reserved capacity options, and schedule a 60-min technical deep dive for private/dedicated lineage.
[08:25] Aisha Khan: i'll collate prompt examples and traffic.
[08:29] Raj Patel: i'll dump p90/p99 histograms and concurrent sessions.
[08:32] Lena Park: perfect. Omar, any final console tips?
[08:35] Omar Sheikh: look at token-level breakdown, enable Optimize suggestions, run the eval suite against your top-25 prompts to guard quality when trying quant models. also set up alerts for p99 drift.
[08:47] Sam Reed: thanks all, that felt useful.
[08:50] Lena Park: thanks everyone for time — we'll follow up with the artifacts and proposed times for the deep dive.
[08:56] [wrap up / small chit-chat] 

Meeting end.
